finding: At the trailing 12-month private-sector separation-rate average of 3.56% per month, a hypothetical employer growing from 1,000 to 1,100 staff needs 548 hires, not 100. The difference is replacement demand under the stated recurrence.
limitations: National industry estimates are not firm-specific turnover probabilities. Total separations include quits, layoffs and other exits. Rates use BLS employment denominators and are rounded. The recurrence instead applies the chosen rate to beginning-month modeled staff, an explicit planning approximation. Same-month hires and exits are not modeled separately. Staffing, growth, capacity and cost inputs are hypothetical. Revised and concurrently seasonally adjusted history is not a real-time vintage backtest. Overlapping three-month targets are dependent, so no significance test or forecast interval is claimed. Latest August estimates are preliminary. Current staffing decisions need company-level evidence.
